title: Nothing reclaims the data that rm leaves behind
details:
`cs-sandbox rm` deliberately keeps a sandbox's home so that `create` with the same name reuses it. `internal/engine/orphan.go` makes that data visible: `ls` shows it with status `removed` and an age, and `destroy` purges it.

What is missing is any pressure to act. Open question 3 in SPEC.md §17 records this as undecided. A host used daily accumulates a microVM `rootfs.ext4` or a `cs-sandbox-home-<name>` volume per removed sandbox, each holding a full home directory, and only a human reading the `ls` output will ever notice.

The pieces for a policy are already there. `Orphan.Since` carries the age, and the Firecracker artifact caches already prune on a TTL that `CS_SANDBOX_FC_REPO_CACHE_TTL_DAYS` controls.

A `prune` verb that purges orphans older than a TTL would follow the pattern the caches already set, and would keep deletion explicit rather than automatic. Reporting the total size that `removed` data occupies would be the smaller first step.
